reading: Stayton Cooperative Telephone Company, doing business as SCTC, is a member owned rural telecommunications cooperative headquartered in Stayton, Oregon, serving the Stayton, Sublimity, and broader Santiam Canyon area. The cooperative was formed on January 14, 1955, through the consolidation of eighteen small independent telephone companies with combined assets of about fifteen thousand dollars at the time. Like many rural telephone cooperatives established in the mid twentieth century, SCTC has since expanded beyond basic telephone service into cable television, added in 1995, long distance service, added in 1999, and fiber based internet and business connectivity today, while retaining its cooperative governance structure in which member customers can vote in elections and serve on the board of directors. The single facility linked to this operator record, tagged as PTC in Linn County, Oregon, is consistent with a telephone central office or exchange building of the kind rural cooperatives operate to serve their member communities, though the specific meaning of the PTC designation was not confirmed from a published source during this research. As a small rural telecommunications cooperative, SCTC's facility functions primarily as network switching infrastructure for its own subscriber base rather than as a commercial colocation data center, and no third party capacity or IT megawattage figures were found or would be expected to exist for a facility of this kind.
